FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Alphabet Tracing Cards A–Z

Twenty-six dotted tracing cards, one for every letter. Numbered arrows show the strokes: start at 1, follow the arrow, lift at the dot. Trace with a finger first — then a crayon, right on the card.

THE CARDS

All twenty-six.

Right here on this page — the full-size card, the words to say together, and the download, print and share buttons.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Little ways that work.

  1. 01

    Start small

    Pick three cards and lay them face up. Three cards is a lovely little class — the whole alphabet can wait.

  2. 02

    Follow the arrows

    Start at the number 1 dot and follow the arrow to the end of the stroke, saying the movement out loud. Then hand the crayon over.

  3. 03

    Tape one up

    Put today’s card at eye level — the fridge, a door. Passing it again and again is quietly powerful practice.

  4. 04

    Match the sets

    Lay a card from this set beside the same card from another letter set and let your child find the pair. The same letter keeps showing up, wearing different clothes.

      FLASHCARD · ALPHABET TRACING CARDS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Letter A Tracing Card — Trace A and a

      A and a in dotted lines, with numbered arrows showing every stroke: start at 1, follow the arrow, lift at the dot. Trace with a finger first — then a crayon. You can draw right on this card.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Trace the letter A: start at the dot, follow the arrow, lift at the end.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the letter, the word, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Finger first, crayon second: trace the dotted A while you say the stroke out loud, then let your child try. The crayons under the picture draw right on the card — save the work when you are done.

      FLASHCARD · ALPHABET TRACING CARDS · AGES 3–4 YEARS
